name: Pabbly Connect
summary: Workflow automation tool that connects apps with webhooks, formatters and API steps. Only actions on outside apps count as tasks, and there is a free plan.
best_for: small teams that run many automations and want to pay per external task instead of per step, with free internal steps
skip_if: you want a large polished app directory with managed email steps and a calm upgrade flow, or you need to cancel and export workflows with confidence before you buy
honest_knock: The free plan has only 100 tasks a month. In our test the email step could not be used without our own SMTP server details, and the first click on Create Workflow opened a full page lifetime offer with a countdown. The upgrade dialog opened on the 3 year plan. Team members are not available on monthly plans, and we did not test support, export or cancelling.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Standard · Standard $19 a month for 10,000 tasks in the upgrade dialog of our own account, read 26 November 2026
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-26 in the Pabbly Connect upgrade dialog, USD) Free: 100 tasks a month, no card asked. Standard: $19 a month for 10,000 tasks, $16 a month billed yearly, $14 a month on a 3 year term. Unlimited: $79 a month, $69 yearly, $59 on a 3 year term. Lifetime deals were offered at $349, $799 and $1,298. The Standard monthly checkout showed Pay $19 with no VAT line. Team members are not available on monthly plans.

compare_with.name: Zapier and Make
compare_with.why: Pabbly Connect charges tasks only for actions on external apps and counts triggers and internal steps as free, which can make high volume workflows cheaper. Zapier and Make are bigger platforms; compare the apps you need, your monthly task volume and how much setup help you want.

claims.claim: Start for free and get 100 tasks - no credit card required.
claims.observed: The dashboard showed Tasks Allotted 100, Tasks Consumed 0, Tasks Remaining 100 on the free plan, and opening Pabbly Connect asked for no card; a card or PayPal was only asked in the upgrade checkout.
claims.comparability: The 100 tasks and the missing card request were both seen on this account; the claim was read on the supplier page and the dashboard in the app.
claims.buying_consequence: The free plan starts with 100 tasks and needs no card to open Pabbly Connect.

claims.claim: Pabbly Connect does not charge tasks for triggers and internal application steps. You're saving 50% on task usage by using Pabbly Connect.
claims.claim_source: In-app tooltip on the Free Task badge, trigger setup, 2026-11-26T08:47:20+01:00
claims.observed: Run 1 (trigger plus Text Formatter) showed Success, 2 Steps Workflow, 2 Free Tasks and 0 Tasks Consumed; the dashboard showed Consumed 0, Remaining 100, Free Tasks Consumed 2.
claims.comparability: The first sentence was tested by a live run of a trigger and one internal step; the 50% saving was not measured.
claims.buying_consequence: A trigger and an internal formatter step did not use any of the 100 free tasks.

claims.claim: Any action performed in your workflow is considered a task. Triggers are not included in the task count, and internal applications of Pabbly Connect, such as filters, routers, and formatters, are also not considered tasks.
claims.observed: Run 2 added an API (Pabbly) step to the trigger and the formatter: 3 Steps Workflow, 1 Tasks Consumed, 4 Free Task Consumed in total; the dashboard then showed Consumed 1, Remaining 99. Filters and routers were not built.
claims.comparability: The trigger and the Text Formatter were seen to be free and the API step cost 1 task; filters and routers were not tested.
claims.buying_consequence: An API request step cost 1 of the 100 free tasks, while the trigger and Text Formatter steps were free.

exit_test.what: On the Free plan of an existing account, one workflow was built with a Catch Webhook trigger, a Text Formatter step (uppercase) and an API (Pabbly) step. It was run live twice and the task counter was read before and after: the trigger and the formatter were free, the API step cost 1 of the 100 free tasks. The email step could not be built without external SMTP credentials. The Standard Monthly checkout showed Pay $19 and was closed before any card data.
exit_test.awkward: Create Workflow opened a full-screen "WAIT! Unlock Your Lifetime Deal" popup with a countdown before the menu could be used; closed it. A top banner throughout read "[LIMITED TIME OFFER] - $194 per year $349 for Lifetime Access" with a countdown. The Upgrade dialog preselected "3 Yearly - SAVE 25%". The only built-in sender is SMTP (Pabbly), which needs SMTP server credentials; there is no Email by Pabbly app.

sessions.what: Our AI assistant ran the test on 26 November 2026 on an existing Pabbly account, with the interface in English. We opened Pabbly Connect, built a webhook to text formatter workflow, added an API step, ran it live twice, read the task counter and opened the upgrade dialog and the Standard monthly checkout. We paid nothing.
findings: Start: Pabbly Connect opened from the Pabbly apps page with one click, no card and no extra form. The dashboard showed 100 tasks allowed and 0 used.
Free steps: the Free Task tooltip said Pabbly does not charge tasks for triggers and internal application steps. Run 1 with trigger and formatter used 0 tasks and counted 2 free ones.
Task count: after run 2 with an API step on our own robots.txt, the dashboard showed 1 task used, 99 left and 4 free tasks used.
Speed: the first result appeared after 3.3 minutes and the first live run after 3.7 minutes.
Email: the email step could not be used without our own SMTP server details; the only built in choice, SMTP (Pabbly), asked for them too.
Upsell: the first click on Create Workflow opened a full page lifetime offer with a countdown, and the upgrade dialog opened on the 3 year plan.
Plans: Standard $19 a month for 10,000 tasks, Unlimited $79; the Standard monthly checkout showed Pay $19 with card or PayPal and no VAT line.
not_tested: paying, the 30 day refund and cancelling
email steps with our own SMTP server
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
